content.overview: Article 102 lists disqualifications for membership of either House of Parliament: office of profit under the Government of India or a State (other than offices exempted by Parliament by law); unsoundness of mind as declared by a competent court; undischarged insolvency; non-citizenship or voluntary foreign allegiance/citizenship; and disqualification under any law made by Parliament (including the Tenth Schedule on defection).
content.glance: Disqualified if: office of profit (unless exempted); unsound mind (court); undischarged insolvent; not a citizen / foreign allegiance; or disqualified under parliamentary law (incl. Tenth Schedule).

sections.heading: Disqualification heads
sections.body:
(a) Office of profit (unless Parliament by law declares it does not disqualify).
(b) Unsound mind (declared by competent court).
(c) Undischarged insolvent.
(d) Not a citizen / voluntary foreign citizenship / foreign allegiance.
(e) Disqualification under any parliamentary law.
Plus: Tenth Schedule (defection) under clause (2).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the disqualifications under Article 102?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 102, a person is disqualified for membership of either House if he holds an office of profit under the Union or a State Government (other than an office exempted by Parliament by law), is of unsound mind as declared by a competent court, is an undischarged insolvent, is not a citizen of India or has voluntarily acquired foreign citizenship or acknowledged allegiance to a foreign State, or is disqualified under any law made by Parliament. Clause (2) adds disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (defection).

examTips: Office of profit; unsound mind; insolvency; citizenship/allegiance; parliamentary law; Tenth Schedule.

keyTakeaways: Art 102: office of profit, mind, insolvency, citizenship, parliamentary law, Tenth Schedule.
